entities.name: Bernardino of Siena
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bernardino of Siena (1380–1444) was an Italian Franciscan priest and the most famous Observant preacher of the early fifteenth century, whose sermons across Italy promoted devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus and moral reform of cities. A systematizer of scholastic economic ethics in preaching, he denounced usury, faction, and luxury while inventing memorable visual and rhetorical tools.

His campaigns helped define Observant Franciscan identity before later controversies over Jew-hatred and civic politics complicated his legacy. Canonised in 1450, he became a model popular preacher of the Quattrocento.

Bernardino shaped urban religion in Renaissance Italy through voice, symbol, and crowd.
